target: Three or more distinct competitive A-band play styles per class in both modes; campaign XVII–XX extremely difficult but beatable. This is an acceptance target, not established parity.

starters.rationale: Reserves and straightforward defense/attacks provide a reliable opening.
Improved Drone and Pulse Pistol help; large-machine setup is still resource hungry.
Pack damage and blood resources are productive early.
Efficient suit/cycling pool gives broad early flexibility; pool parity unresolved.
Recurring Dagger and efficient Skills provide consistent damage.
Two starting totems offer immediate value before row investment.
Stance sequencing is strong but mistakes can expose the hero.
Starting Spell Power supplies an early spend/rebuild rhythm.
Small Thralls and slower Fate/Consume development need protection.
Gun and drink setup can compete, but HP/Hangover management is less forgiving.

basis: Theorycraft assessment of plausible developed decks at comparable upgrade quality. No balance simulations or real-match dataset used. Grades include the class pool and base trait; the marginal Ascendancy is discussed separately. A deterministic fixture establishes behavior, never a win-rate or a tier grade.

ratings.name: Paladin
ratings.scaling: 60% retained Barrier compounds only when generation exceeds incoming pressure
ratings.rationale: Retention gives useful defense immediately and supports scaled Barrier attacks later. Strong late potential depends on converting defense into damage.
ratings.watch: Piercing damage, direct HP loss and slow kills against scaling foes.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Marshal
ratings.scaling: Up to +40% attack damage from actual Reserves spent that turn
ratings.rationale: The extra Reserve and percentage payoff grow with upgraded attacks, rather than adding a fixed early-only bonus.
ratings.watch: Time spent banking; the opening hand may not access Reserves efficiently.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Blood Knight
ratings.scaling: First real payment +10 percentage points, within 30/round and 60 stored
ratings.rationale: A meaningful payment now charges even at large Arena HP. The real-HP-loss rate remains and the bank boosts all hits of the next Attack.
ratings.watch: Multi-hit burst stacking; campaign attrition and healing access.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Swarmwright
ratings.build: Many small summons / continuous attack bonuses
ratings.scaling: +1 damage per hit per 3 successful new summons, four slots, 1 Primed per companion
ratings.rationale: Earlier Fabrication improves ordinary swarm growth. Consume recycling prevents the former repeatable free loop from defining its ceiling.
ratings.watch: Area damage, summoning Mana costs, command density; unrestricted copy/reclaim engines still need observation.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Golemancer
ratings.scaling: +3 companion max HP/turn; +1% large-machine attack per max HP, capped +100%
ratings.rationale: Recovery reduces the loss of a grown machine without removing the existing HP-to-damage conversion. It still needs time and a replacement card.
ratings.watch: Focused companion removal and setup time remain its largest uncertainties; recovery does not refund summon Mana.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Artillerist
ratings.scaling: +1 Might each own turn, first Attack 3 Barrier
ratings.rationale: Weapon damage grows without depending on a fragile summon board. Continuous friendly attack bonuses can support a hybrid list.
ratings.watch: Rotary Cannon and Primed stacking; generic draw and Mana access.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Beastmaster
ratings.scaling: 75% Might sharing makes each companion hit scale
ratings.rationale: Might investment is multiplied across a pack; this remains a distinct board-focused option beside burst Hunter decks.
ratings.watch: Board wipes, ally slots and protecting newly built companions.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Reaver
ratings.recovery: Moderate; hero HP is the resource
ratings.scaling: First own HP payment each turn draws 1 and grants 2 Primed
ratings.rationale: Cheap blood cards convert risk into tempo. Its unchanged pool may still make it an upper-band option.
ratings.watch: Flat HP payments at Arena HP; pool efficiency remains unresolved.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Predator
ratings.scaling: First 6 additional draws give 2 Primed; later draws give 1
ratings.rationale: Normal draw turns keep their payoff while extreme draw chains grow at half the former marginal rate. Large burst remains intentional.
ratings.watch: One Attack cashes all Primed; free draw chains remain a card-pool risk.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Trapmaster
ratings.recovery: Good if traps can be reset
ratings.scaling: Each sprung Trap draws 1 and gives 2 Barrier
ratings.rationale: Reactive cycling supports defense and deck access; opponents must actually trigger the trap conditions.
ratings.watch: Skill-heavy opponents and avoided traps reduce both defense and draw.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Cardsharp
ratings.scaling: Full Trick also grants 1 Mana, on top of class suit rewards
ratings.rationale: Suit completion rewards sequencing and keeps developed decks moving. No new card-pool restrictions are introduced.
ratings.watch: Class pool may offer too much cheap draw/Mana; Ascendancy parity cannot settle that concern alone.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Seer
ratings.scaling: Marked target +10% per qualifying turn to +50%, with first aimed Attack Exposed
ratings.rationale: Percentage pressure has a late payoff and starts with a real debuff. Long single-target fights favor it.
ratings.watch: Frequent target changes and untargeted damage lower the payoff.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Bladedancer
ratings.scaling: One extra Dagger every turn scales with Edge/Might and on-play effects
ratings.rationale: Recurring attacks make per-hit growth valuable and provide consistent engine fuel.
ratings.watch: Efficient neutral Mana/draw and rare multipliers may keep the best decks above the intended band.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Bloodletter
ratings.scaling: Enemy Bleed/Burn ticks one extra time each turn, decaying for each tick
ratings.rationale: Persistent damage ignores ordinary Attack scaling and rewards maintained stacks rather than one burst turn.
ratings.watch: Cleanse timing, Fate races, and how often humans take existing counterplay.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Assassin
ratings.scaling: +15% per finished Skill up to +60%, plus additive +20% below half target HP
ratings.rationale: A flexible burst path with a clear setup/payoff sequence and wounded-target finisher.
ratings.watch: Does the next Attack reliably deserve the stored boost, including multi-hit effects?
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Totemist
ratings.recovery: Moderate; row and Spirit need rebuilding
ratings.scaling: +1 Spirit per qualifying no-command turn with 2+ totems; starts 1 Spirit/8 Barrier
ratings.rationale: Standing rows can develop without consuming their investments. This does not gain Storm Sovereign activations from passive effects.
ratings.watch: Long passive rows can overtake flat defenses; compare real command versus cultivation decisions.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Spiritwalker
ratings.scaling: First command/push-out each turn draws 1 and gives 4 Barrier
ratings.rationale: A valuable consistent cycling reward remains. The shared Storm Sovereign cost and Barrier limit reduce the strongest command engine's sustain.
ratings.watch: Earlier S rating overstated Sovereign's passive scope; unchanged trigger itself is only once per turn.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Elementalist
ratings.scaling: First of each element/turn grows by 1 per prior trigger, switching adds 2
ratings.rationale: Three separately growing elemental rewards support a flexible sequence deck without a mandatory standing row.
ratings.watch: Hand diversity and how often all three elements can be triggered safely.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Sage
ratings.scaling: First Serene exit each turn gives 1 extra Mana
ratings.rationale: A reliable resource bonus supports the base stance engine and lets larger upgraded cards fit into a turn.
ratings.watch: Cheap stance cycling and card-pool efficiency; extra Mana is only useful with cards to spend it on.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Zealot
ratings.build: Controlled Fury / entry and exit growth
ratings.recovery: Good if a safe exit is available
ratings.scaling: First own-turn Fury entry +8% to +40%; first exit 4+2 per earned step Barrier
ratings.rationale: Deliberate Fury exposure develops damage and a growing exit defense. Its risk is different from Serene or Radiant resource play.
ratings.watch: Being trapped in Fury; incoming damage pressure and exit-card consistency.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Sunwalker
ratings.recovery: Moderate; must reach another Radiant window
ratings.scaling: First stance entry extra Fervor; Radiant exit returns 2, then 3, then 4
ratings.rationale: Investment reduces the cost of later Radiant cycles, supporting strong developed fights.
ratings.watch: Too few early stance tools or repeated Radiant turns overwhelming other damage paths.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Blademaster
ratings.scaling: +1 per Sword hit and first Sword each turn draws 1
ratings.rationale: Consistent throughput and card access; multi-hit cards keep a fixed Keen point useful later.
ratings.watch: A fixed bonus can lag percentage builds unless the Sword deck has enough hits.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Archmage
ratings.scaling: First spending Spell Attack +1 per spent Power per hit; half refunded next turn
ratings.rationale: A resource investment produces a scalable burst and partial recovery instead of fixed damage alone.
ratings.watch: Extreme multi-hit expenditure and whether refund timing creates too much free late power.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Shatterer
ratings.scaling: +15% Shatter damage; Fault Lines gives 2 Fracture for first 6 qualifying plays, then 1
ratings.rationale: The growing payoff remains, while large free-play turns create Fracture more slowly. Cleansing cannot remove Fracture.
ratings.watch: Permanent Fracture plus many cheap plays may still be an outlier; opponent pressure is the real counterplay.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Bonelord
ratings.scaling: Extra Raise 2 each turn, +2 companion damage, on top of class Raise
ratings.rationale: Stronger recurring bodies and per-hit damage help commands compete without needing the Consume engine.
ratings.watch: Arena companion HP remains small beside hero HP; focus fire and late multi-enemy damage.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Fateweaver
ratings.scaling: 2 Fate +2% target max HP at own turn start
ratings.rationale: Percentage Fate remains relevant at large enemy HP and Arena HP. It is a delayed execution threshold, not immediate damage.
ratings.watch: Random targets, cleanse and immunity timing; percentage contribution should not be counted twice as ordinary damage.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Soulreaper
ratings.scaling: First 6 Consume/owner-round +1 Harvest/3 Barrier; one Reap 4+2 Harvest on qualifying own turns
ratings.rationale: A normal three-Consume turn still gives 9 Barrier and reaches Reap 52 on turn eight. Extreme single-round feeding no longer grants unlimited growth.
ratings.watch: Six consumes each round still reaches Reap 100 by turn eight; generation quality and Grave Chill may keep this path above A.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Brewmaster
ratings.recovery: Good once paid growth is established
ratings.scaling: First actual own-turn Hangover payment adds a step to 5; each heals 1% max HP and gives 2 Barrier
ratings.rationale: Sustain grows with hero HP and does not depend on making ever-larger Hangover piles. The payment is a real setup cost.
ratings.watch: Percentage healing at Arena HP, actual payment avoidance and setup survival.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Gunslinger
ratings.recovery: Good; weapon copies grow each turn
ratings.scaling: Gun starts +3 Precision and gains +2 each own turn
ratings.rationale: Weapon investment keeps scaling through extended fights without requiring low HP or Hangover payments.
ratings.watch: Draw access to the gun and whether Precision scaling beats other weapon engines at comparable deck quality.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

ratings.name: Deathwish
ratings.recovery: Limited; one rescue buys a brief window
ratings.scaling: Extra Attack bonus ramps below 70% to +25% at 40%; one hostile lethal rescue
ratings.rationale: The ramp supplies payoff before the dangerous lowest band, and broader rescue closes the Skill/DoT hole. Multi-hit follow-ups remain dangerous.
ratings.watch: Its A− estimate has low confidence: healing conflicts with the HP band and campaign attrition is real.
evidence: Authored rule/card review and hand costing

corrections: All 30 estimates fall in the A band overall; Golemancer and Deathwish remain low-confidence A−, not proven repaired matchups.
Opening grades can remain B+ for a slow build while its complete-deck estimate is A−; no claim that every opening hand is equally strong.
No measured playtests used. Do not manufacture win rates or turn fixture success into A-tier evidence.
Storm Sovereign still does not trigger from passive effects; damage is uncapped, only Barrier is limited per copy.
Card-pool parity remains unresolved. Efficient draw/Mana, rare access, seat order, player skill, deck size and campaign investment affect results.
Reroll uses original odds and can show repeated cards. It improves choice access, not guaranteed synergy or rarity.
Build examples are descriptive, not predefined reward groups or an exhaustive list of viable decks.
